documents.title: GRC Professional Workday Analysis — August 3 OSINT Sweep
documents.executiveSummary: Ironintel and Ironwatch live OSINT for August 3, 2026 pivots from August 2 identity-first convergence to MSP supply-chain cascade: N-able disclosed CVE-2026-18577 August 2 after incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556 — unauthenticated authentication bypass grants god-mode RMM console access on N-central builds prior to 2026.3.1.7, enabling Take Control lateral movement, Cloudflare tunnel persistence via cloudflared services, and downstream compromise across all managed customer endpoints; Huntress confirmed exploitation across nine organizations under one partner account August 3. WordPress Core CVE-2026-60137 BOD 26-04 FCEB deadline arrives August 4 (1 day remaining). CMMC Phase II C3PAO suspension enters day 21 of 60-day Reform Task Force review (report due September 11; industry RFI closes August 14 with 11 days remaining). Carryover priorities: CaptiveCrunch Storm-2945 traveler token theft, Arch AUR developer supply-chain freeze, ShinyHunters healthcare SSO extortion, Minnesota water PLC day seven, Cl0p Windchill PLM extortion, and post-deadline Cisco FMC forensic attestation.
keyFindings: N-able N-central RMM god-mode authentication bypass August 2–3, 2026 — CVE-2026-18577 (CVSS 8.2) results from incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556; unauthenticated remote attackers gain administrative account takeover on N-central versions through 2026.3.1 across hosted and on-premises MSP deployments; post-exploitation leverages Take Control for downstream endpoint access and registers Cloudflare tunnel (cloudflared) services for persistence after N-central access revocation; hotfix 2026.3.1.7 released August 2; Huntress August 3 rapid response confirms exploitation across nine customer organizations under one self-hosted partner instance — Technology, Finance, and Healthcare Industry Profiles relying on MSP-managed RMM must verify build 2026.3.1.7, hunt cloudflared services and svchost.exe anomalies in user document folders, and restrict N-central console to VPN-only administrative access.

WordPress Core CVE-2026-60137 BOD 26-04 deadline day August 3 — SQL injection KEV (added July 21) requires FCEB remediation by August 4 (1 day remaining); EPSS 79.0 percent; Technology and Public Sector Industry Profiles must execute emergency patch cycle on internet-facing CMS estates before CaptiveCrunch identity triage deferrals.

ragChunks.section: Active Threat Vector — N-able N-central RMM God-Mode Authentication Bypass
ragChunks.text: Ironwatch OSINT 2026-08-03: N-able disclosed CVE-2026-18577 August 2 after incomplete patch for CVE-2026-18556. Unauthenticated remote attackers achieve administrative account takeover on N-central versions through 2026.3.1 across hosted and on-premises MSP deployments. Post-exploitation leverages Take Control for downstream endpoint access and registers Cloudflare tunnel (cloudflared) services for persistence after N-central access revocation. Hotfix 2026.3.1.7 released August 2. Huntress August 3 rapid response confirms exploitation across nine customer organizations under one self-hosted partner instance reaching one endpoint in each. Known malicious IPs include 173.249.252.200, 87.249.138.34, 37.19.210.32, 68.235.46.214, 37.153.90.88, and 92.118.112.181. Known domains: mousears.synology.me, wagoosh.direct.quickconnect.to, who-ripped-one.direct.quickconnect.to. Finland NCSC-FI issued advisory August 2. Technology, Finance, and Healthcare Industry Profiles relying on MSP-managed RMM must verify build 2026.3.1.7, hunt cloudflared services, restrict console to VPN-only access, and enforce MFA.

ragChunks.section: Active Threat Vector — CaptiveCrunch Midnight Blizzard Captive Portal Campaign
ragChunks.text: Ironwatch OSINT 2026-08-03 carryover: Microsoft Threat Intelligence disclosed CaptiveCrunch campaign attributed to Storm-2945 (Midnight Blizzard sub-cluster). Since early May 2026, threat actors manipulate DNS and HTTP traffic on hotel, conference, and shared-venue captive portals worldwide. CornFlake RAT and ChocoShell harvest Microsoft 365, Azure AD access tokens, refresh tokens, and WAM tokens from Token Broker cache. Device-code phishing added mid-July redirects users into legitimate Microsoft authentication where user completes MFA for attacker session. Microsoft recommends blocking device-code flow via Conditional Access. ReliaQuest corroborated July 23. Defense, Finance, Technology, and Public Sector profiles with traveling workforce must enforce VPN-before-Wi-Fi and hunt Token Broker anomalies on returning endpoints.
